output.name: Cartoon fact shorts
output.description: Use when making a ~30 s vertical 3D-rendered fact or true-story short: a fast deadpan narrator walks through a cause-and-effect chain while a camera that almost never stops shows each fact as a literal picture.
output.summary: These are 9:16 shorts of about 29 s. They use a clean, semi-real 3D render with no outlines. One deadpan narrator talks almost without a break: 196 wpm while speaking, 172 wpm across the whole video, and speech covering about 88% of the runtime. The script opens on the consequence or the action already happening, with a concrete count. It then chains cause to effect and ends on the outcome, with no outro. Sets and figures stay frozen like dioramas. Nearly all the energy comes from the camera. It moves in about 88% of frames, makes one move on one axis per shot, arrives about 2.4× faster than it cruises, and passes to the following shot through 5–6 frame blur, zoom-through or whip transitions. A new picture appears about every 1.9 s. Every fact becomes its own literal close-up: counters for numbers, a morph for a comparison, a cutaway for a hidden process. Short action bursts of about 4 frames sit on their verbs. The only overlay is a small white caption at 78% of frame height, swapped in 2–4 word chunks. The last frame echoes the first, so the video loops softly.

sections.title: Format & pace
sections.intro: Short, dense and always moving. Times come from the table's medians across the two references.

rules.title: Length
rules.default: About 29.3 s, 9:16. Narration starts on frame 1. The last word lands 0.5–0.8 s before the end.
rules.deviateWhen: never go past about 31 s. Trim words before slowing the voice.
rules.why: Short enough that it runs out before attention does, and it loops cleanly.

rules.title: Picture rate
rules.default: A new picture about every 1.9 s (median 1.88 s), carrying about 4 spoken words.
rules.range: 1.5–2.2 s average; individual shots run 0.3–3.9 s (p10–p90); 2–6.5 words per picture
rules.deviateWhen: For a line that lists or counts parts, run a burst of 4–6 inserts at 6–12 frames each, about 1 word per shot. For results, impacts and explanations, use long single-move shots of 3–4.8 s carrying 10–14 words.
rules.why: The eye gets something new before the ear finishes the thought.

rules.title: First change
rules.default: First picture change at about 1.7 s, on the word that names who or what is affected.
rules.deviateWhen: If the hook names the viewer or the people at risk early, cut on that word, even if it comes before 1 s.
rules.why: Moves from the threat or subject straight to the stakes.

rules.title: Two-speed rhythm
rules.default: Alternate quick decisive shots of 1–1.6 s with longer result shots of 3–3.7 s. Never run a whole video at one shot length.
rules.range: Shot lengths run from 6 frames to about 4.8 s inside one video
rules.deviateWhen: The hinge beat gets the shortest shot; the aftermath or explanation gets the longest.
rules.why: The contrast in tempo shows what matters.

rules.title: No opening card, no outro
rules.default: Open on picture and voice together, and end on the last outcome word. No opening text card, no outro, no call to action.
rules.deviateWhen: never
rules.why: Every second goes to the story.

sections.title: Script & hook
sections.intro: About 80–90 words: a deadpan chain of causes that pays off the hook at the very end.

rules.title: Hook
rules.default: One declarative sentence of 11–14 words, ending at about 4.7 s. It puts the subject or threat already in action and includes a concrete count.
rules.deviateWhen: never open with a question or 'did you know'.
rules.why: Puts the stakes and a number in front of the viewer before they can scroll away.

rules.title: Structure
rules.default: 3–5 sentences, about 84 words in total. Order: hook with the count, a long chained setup or escalation (the longest sentence, spread over the most shots), the turn, then the outcome.
rules.deviateWhen: For a process explainer, use 3 sentences, with the last one starting on a sequence word such as 'Then'. For a true story, use 5 beats: threat, small unrelated action, what it caused, the threat strikes, the payoff.
rules.why: Cause and effect pulls the viewer toward the answer.

rules.title: Chained clauses
rules.default: Join steps with cause or time links (so, while, until, as, which, minutes later) and with -ing result clauses. Use one blunt physical verb per step.
rules.deviateWhen: Save 'But' for the twist and the payoff only.
rules.why: No sentence ever feels finished, so the pace never stops.

rules.title: Voice of the script
rules.default: Plain and deadpan, with no opinion words and no jokes.
rules.range: third-person past tense (true story) to second-person present with the viewer as the object of the action (explainer)
rules.deviateWhen: Use 'you' only when the viewer is the subject of the process, and then use it throughout.
rules.why: Delivered flat, the facts feel like documentary.

rules.title: Literal comparisons
rules.default: Pair any unfamiliar part or mechanism with one familiar everyday object it works like, so it can be drawn.
rules.deviateWhen: Skip comparisons in a story that has no unfamiliar mechanism.
rules.why: Gives the picture something concrete to show.

rules.title: Ending and loop line
rules.default: The last sentence states the outcome and ends on its key word. Where possible, that word repeats the word that ends the hook.
rules.range: verbal echo present in 1 of 2 references
rules.deviateWhen: In a process piece, end on the final physical action instead.
rules.why: Closes the hook and invites a replay.

sections.title: Voice & sound
sections.intro: One fast narrator over a quiet, flat music bed, mastered loud.

rules.title: Speaking rate
rules.default: 196 wpm while speaking and 172 wpm across the whole video, with speech covering about 88% of the runtime. No gaps between words inside a clause.
rules.deviateWhen: never slow down for emphasis. Use pitch instead.
rules.why: The density is the energy of the style.

rules.title: Pauses
rules.default: About 0.37 s after a sentence and 0.34 s after a clause.
rules.range: sentence 0.3–0.4 s (up to 0.55 s); clause 0.3–0.4 s
rules.deviateWhen: Before the payoff sentence, leave the longest gap, about 0.6 s.
rules.why: Just enough air to mark structure without losing pace.

rules.title: Delivery
rules.default: Deadpan and news-like, median pitch about 171 Hz, pitch range about 15.7 semitones. Lift the pitch on the hook, the twist word and the impact verb.
rules.range: 165–176 Hz; 14.6–16.8 semitones (may be inflated by the music)
rules.deviateWhen: never act out emotion or laugh.
rules.why: Flat delivery plus pitch peaks makes the facts land.

rules.title: Music bed
rules.default: One steady bed about 12.7 dB under the voice. No swells and no audible ducking. Fade out right after the last word.
rules.deviateWhen: never add a drop or a swell.
rules.why: Keeps momentum without competing with the words.

rules.title: Loudness
rules.default: Master to about -10 LUFS with a narrow loudness range (about 2 LU). True peak at or below -1 dBFS.
rules.deviateWhen: never let true peak go above -1 dBFS. Both references clip; don't copy that.
rules.why: Loud on a phone without distortion.

rules.title: Sound effects
rules.default: Optional: one short hit per key object or event (whoosh on whips, impact on the key action), mixed under the voice.
rules.range: inferred from the picture only, not measured
rules.deviateWhen: Drop them if they mask any word.
rules.why: Adds weight to the moment the picture shows.

sections.title: Look
sections.intro: Clean semi-real 3D. Despite the style's name, it does not use cartoon shading.

rules.title: Render
rules.default: Semi-real 3D with physically plausible materials, crisp highlights, fine surface detail and soft background depth of field.
rules.deviateWhen: never add outlines, toon bands, cel shading or film grain.
rules.why: Reads as documentary but stays simple enough to read at a glance.

rules.title: Palette
rules.default: A limited palette per scene, with the saturated accent reserved for the key object or the protagonists.
rules.range: dark and muted (near-black interiors, flat grey threat exteriors) to bright and complementary (warm subject against a cool sky, an all-warm interior)
rules.deviateWhen: Use dark and muted for danger or true stories, bright for explainers. When a consequence hits, tint the subject a hot emissive colour over 3 frames, 0–15 frames after the key word.
rules.why: The eye goes straight to what the narrator is talking about.

rules.title: Lighting
rules.default: One clear key light on the subject. Self-lit displays glow.
rules.range: overhead pool on the subject with surroundings falling to dark, to bright soft top or front key with sky fill
rules.deviateWhen: Use overcast, flat light for threat exteriors.
rules.why: Isolates the subject and sets the mood with no extra elements.

rules.title: Sets
rules.default: One readable place per shot with no stray props: a dense full-scale place for scale shots, a sparse surface for close work.
rules.range: packed crowds and aerial wides, to a single curved surface under a gradient sky
rules.deviateWhen: For hidden or internal events, cut to a frame-filling cross-section. For the hinge beat, use the key object alone on pure black (about 96% black).
rules.why: Every shot has one obvious subject.

rules.title: Caption-safe composition
rules.default: Keep the subject in the centre column, within about 10% of the width. Keep the band at 75–80% of frame height mid-to-dark and low in detail.
rules.deviateWhen: never put bright, busy detail behind the caption.
rules.why: Caption and subject never fight.

sections.title: Characters & faces
sections.intro: People are stand-ins. Posture or objects do the acting, not faces.

rules.title: Stand-in figures
rules.default: Realistic proportions (about 7 heads tall) and simple features. Reuse one model across shots, dressed in one repeated outfit in a single bright colour.
rules.range: used in many shots (true story) down to a single scale shot (explainer)
rules.deviateWhen: In an explainer, show a human once, only for scale or for 'you'.
rules.why: Viewers read them as the same people with no introduction.

rules.title: Faces
rules.default: Small (about 1/15 of frame height), neutral and fixed, or hidden. No lip sync, no blinks, no expression changes.
rules.deviateWhen: never
rules.why: Emotion goes into pose and camera, which keeps the render cheap and the tone deadpan.

rules.title: Faceless subjects
rules.default: When the subject is an object or creature, it acts through what it does and through material or colour changes, never through a face.
rules.deviateWhen: never add cartoon eyes or mouths.
rules.why: Keeps the documentary tone.

rules.title: Crowds
rules.default: Show a claim about many people as two or three recurring figures doing the action, set inside a dense crowd.
rules.deviateWhen: Wide scale shots may show the full crowd frozen.
rules.why: Makes a number feel personal.

sections.title: Motion & acting
sections.intro: Frozen dioramas broken by short mechanical bursts.

rules.title: Frozen holds
rules.default: Between beats, figures and props are dead still (0.01 px/frame leftover motion). No idle, breathing or drift.
rules.deviateWhen: never
rules.why: The camera carries all continuity, so stillness reads as a deliberate tableau.

rules.title: Action bursts
rules.default: About 7 motion bursts per 10 s (6.77), each about 4 frames (4.25).
rules.deviateWhen: For one climax body action, use 9–11 frames with ease-in-out, then hold. Allow at most one per video.
rules.why: Quick hits punctuate the narration without slowing it.

rules.title: Timing to the word
rules.default: Start an illustrative action 1–5 frames before its word.
rules.range: from 5 frames before to 3 frames after the word; aftermath beats 6–13 frames after
rules.deviateWhen: Start repeated loops (pumping, sawing, pulsing) 10–12 frames before the verb that names them.
rules.why: The picture confirms the word as it is heard.

rules.title: No anticipation, no overshoot
rules.default: Linear or ease-in moves straight into the key pose. Hand off to a camera move or a hold, never a settle.
rules.deviateWhen: never
rules.why: Mechanical precision fits the deadpan voice.

rules.title: Poses tell emotion
rules.default: One readable pose per figure per shot: slumped for despair, upright for waiting, crouched for danger.
rules.deviateWhen: When an action carries into a second shot, open that shot already in the key pose, hold 2–3 frames, then transition out.
rules.why: Emotion reads at once with no face animation.

rules.title: Fast elements
rules.default: Put fast motion into particles crossing a static set, at about 10–20% of frame height per frame (estimated by eye). Keep threats slow and hazy before impact.
rules.deviateWhen: Only at or after the impact beat.
rules.why: Violence reads through particles while the scene stays readable.

sections.title: Camera
sections.intro: The camera is the performer. Speeds come from the table's medians.

rules.title: Always moving
rules.default: The camera moves in about 88% of frames. Each shot gets one continuous move on one axis (push-in by default, otherwise a pan or tilt), never reversed.
rules.deviateWhen: never reverse inside a shot.
rules.why: Constant motion holds attention while the set stays still.

rules.title: Cruise speed
rules.default: About 23.5 %/s mid-shot, made up of about 8.8 %/s zoom and 8.6 %/s pan.
rules.deviateWhen: Short inserts creep at 5–8 %/s. A large establishing or threat shot gets one steady 40–50% zoom over 3–4 s.
rules.why: Steady drift, never jittery.

rules.title: Arrive fast, leave moving
rules.default: Enter each shot about 2.4× cruise speed and ease out to cruise over 6–18 frames. In the last 8–15 frames, speed up to about 1.2× cruise on the same axis.
rules.range: arrival 1.9–2.8× (single shots up to about 28×); exit 1.0–1.3× (single shots up to 5–7×)
rules.deviateWhen: When the shot ends in a whip or zoom-through, ramp hard into it so the move is already fast when the transition starts.
rules.why: Momentum carries across the join.

rules.title: Smooth paths
rules.default: Spline-smooth moves with no handheld noise. Measured shake was about 0.27 % of frame per frame, but it comes from particles and texture, not the camera, so aim for zero.
rules.deviateWhen: never add simulated shake.
rules.why: Clean moves keep the documentary-render feel.

rules.title: One hold
rules.default: At most one near-still shot per video: the hinge object or the explanatory beat.
rules.range: from about 1.1 s (hinge object on black) to about 4 s (explanation at 0.1 %/s)
rules.deviateWhen: Leave the hold by easing up to about 50 %/s over its last 10 frames.
rules.why: A single pause in a moving film marks the turning point.

rules.title: Reveals
rules.default: Rack focus from soft to sharp over about 10 frames, finishing 3–6 frames before the subject is named.
rules.deviateWhen: Alternatively, tilt across a textured surface so the following subject enters over the frame edge 8–10 frames before the transition.
rules.why: The viewer finds the subject just as it is named.

rules.title: Final move
rules.default: The last shot pulls out and slows to almost zero (about 0.2–1.9 %/s) on the last word.
rules.deviateWhen: never end on a fast move.
rules.why: Lands the outcome and sets up the loop.

sections.title: Cuts & transitions
sections.intro: Shots are joined by motion, mostly.

rules.title: Mix
rules.default: About 76% motion transitions (blur, zoom-through, whip) and 24% hard or near-hard cuts.
rules.range: motion 58.8–92.3%; hard cuts 7.7–41.2% (the higher figure counts 1–2 frame snap moves as cuts)
rules.deviateWhen: Use 1–2 frame snap moves instead of plain cuts inside a burst of inserts.
rules.why: The camera never feels like it was switched off.

rules.title: Blur length
rules.default: About 6 frames of directional blur (median 5.75).
rules.deviateWhen: Zoom-throughs 5–7 frames; whips 3–9 frames (default 5).
rules.why: Long enough to feel the move, short enough not to blur a word.

rules.title: Zoom-through
rules.default: Keep the zoom direction on both sides. Push into a dark surface (1–2 near-black frames), then reveal the following shot still pushing, with radial blur. Change scale by 3–5× or at least one shot-size step.
rules.deviateWhen: Moving from exterior to interior, push or tilt through the surface. Coming back out, reverse the move.
rules.why: Reads as one continuous journey.

rules.title: Whip
rules.default: A pan or tilt at 5–9 % of frame per frame with linear streak blur along that axis. The new subject is sharp within 4 frames, ideally on a word's first frame.
rules.deviateWhen: Where possible, whip between two objects in the same space.
rules.why: Connects cause and consequence in one gesture.

rules.title: Placement
rules.default: Change pictures mid-sentence, never on a sentence end. Only about 11% of changes fall on clause starts (chance is about 8–9%).
rules.range: new picture readable 0–4 frames before its noun, to the change landing 4–12 frames into the word
rules.deviateWhen: never cut on a sentence boundary.
rules.why: Picture and voice overlap, so there is no dead beat.

rules.title: Dissolves
rules.default: No plain crossfades between shots.
rules.range: directional-blur dissolves of 3–6 frames appear in 1 of 2 references
rules.deviateWhen: For a pull-out, you may run a 4–6 frame blurred dissolve while both shots zoom out, with the clean frame landing on a word onset.
rules.why: Every join still feels like camera motion.

sections.title: Captions & graphics
sections.intro: One small caption is the only overlay.

rules.title: Caption style
rules.default: Small white bold sans, centred, baseline at about 78% of frame height, letters 3–4% of frame height, soft dark drop shadow.
rules.range: lowercase or sentence case; a 4-word line up to about 70% of width
rules.deviateWhen: never add a box, a heavy outline or an emphasis colour.
rules.why: Readable with sound off without competing with the picture.

rules.title: Chunks
rules.default: 2–4 word groups with punctuation removed. Hard 1-frame swaps within ±3 frames of the chunk's first word.
rules.deviateWhen: Hold one chunk across a burst of fast inserts and through pauses.
rules.why: Follows the voice without flicker.

rules.title: Layering
rules.default: Composite captions above the transitions so they stay sharp and fixed while the picture blurs. Keep the top 15% and bottom 18% free of text.
rules.deviateWhen: never
rules.why: Gives a steady anchor through every move.

rules.title: No overlays
rules.default: No labels, arrows, icons, maps, lower thirds or text cards. Every number appears on an in-world display.
rules.deviateWhen: never
rules.why: The render explains, and the screen stays clean.

sections.title: Facts into pictures
sections.intro: Every claim gets a literal shot, timed to its word.

rules.title: One fact, one close-up
rules.default: Give each mechanism, time or rule its own close-up of the thing doing it, readable at the word that names it.
rules.deviateWhen: When the script counts parts, fan them out in a burst of inserts, one per part.
rules.why: The viewer sees every claim, not just hears it.

rules.title: Numbers on in-world displays
rules.default: Show times, scores and counts on glowing self-lit displays that fill 60–70% of frame width. Swap a value as an instant 1-frame change about 10 frames after it is named, once the camera has settled.
rules.deviateWhen: never use overlay numbers.
rules.why: Numbers stay inside the world and stay readable.

rules.title: Literal comparison morph
rules.default: Morph the part into the compared object with a 3-frame dissolve starting 0–2 frames before the comparison word. Hold 15–20 frames, then dissolve back over 3 frames.
rules.deviateWhen: Only when the script makes a comparison.
rules.why: Turns an analogy into an image.

rules.title: Show the hidden
rules.default: For an internal process, turn the surface translucent or drain it over 2–3 frames, 3–5 frames before the verb, then animate the inside on the verb.
rules.deviateWhen: Or cut to a cross-section set.
rules.why: Makes the invisible step visible right when it is named.

rules.title: Hinge object
rules.default: At the turning point, isolate the key object or action in a short, near-still, uncluttered shot.
rules.range: object on pure black for about 1.1 s, to a ~4 s still explanatory frame
rules.deviateWhen: Only once per video.
rules.why: Marks the moment everything hinges on.

rules.title: Loop picture
rules.default: End on a wide shot that echoes the opening composition (last-to-first frame correlation about 0.61).
rules.deviateWhen: For a stronger loop, return to the opening place and angle exactly.
rules.why: The replay feels seamless.

checklist: Runtime is 27.6–31.1 s, there is no opening text card or outro, and the last word lands 0.5–0.8 s before the end.
The hook is one declarative sentence with a concrete count, ending by about 4.7 s, with no question.
The first picture change comes at 0.9–2.5 s, on the word naming who or what is affected.
Narration runs at about 196 wpm while speaking and covers about 86–89% of the runtime, with about 0.35 s pauses.
A new picture appears about every 1.5–2.2 s, and no shot change falls on a sentence boundary.
The camera moves in about 85–91% of frames, with one non-reversing move per shot and at most one hold.
Each shot arrives about 2× faster than its cruise speed (about 19–28 %/s), and the final shot slows to a stop.
At least about 60% of transitions are blur, zoom-through or whip moves of about 5–6 frames. There are no plain crossfades.
Figures and props are frozen between ~4-frame action bursts. No faces animate, and nothing has anticipation or overshoot.
Every fact has its own literal close-up. Numbers appear on in-world displays, and there are no overlay graphics.
Captions are small, white, 2–4 words, at about 78% height, hard-swapped within ±3 frames, and stay sharp over transitions.
The mix is about -10 LUFS, true peak ≤ -1 dBFS, music about 11–15 dB under the voice, and the last frame echoes the first.
avoid: Hard cuts as the default join, or plain crossfades between shots
Reversing the camera direction inside a shot
More than one camera hold per video
Outlines, toon or cel shading, flat cartoon colours or film grain
Lip sync, blinks, expression changes or cartoon faces on objects
Idle breathing, drift or fidgeting between action beats
Overlay graphics: labels, arrows, icons, maps, lower thirds or text cards
Kinetic captions, word pop-ins, caption boxes, heavy outlines or emphasis colours
Jokes, opinion words, morals, outros or calls to action
Cutting on sentence boundaries, or gaps between words inside a clause
Cluttered sets that hide the one subject or crowd the caption band
